text: Your first Monday without an office. The alarm still goes off at 6:30 out of habit, even though you're your own boss now. Rise and grind like a real founder?
Your co-founder Gosha calls at 7:15: "I came up with a name overnight. It rhymes with our product, just not in any language we speak." He's thrilled. Hear him out?
Your old boss texts: "If the startup doesn't take off, your desk is yours till the end of the month." Sweet, and slightly insulting. Reply?
Time to register the company. A consultant will handle it in a week for a fee, or you can do it yourself in one day of queues. Your call?
The office is currently your kitchen table. Your co-founder is still here at night, and your family wants dinner on that exact table. Now what?
An angel investor you know can do breakfast — only today, 7:30, across town. You don't have a deck yet, just an idea and a napkin. Go?
Gosha suggests a 50/50 equity split. He writes the code, but the idea and every negotiation are yours. Time for the talk. Have it now?
The perfect domain is taken. The owner wants a month's rent for it. An ugly hyphenated version is free. Decide.
Mom calls in the evening: "I told the neighbor you're a businessperson now. She's asking if you can hire her grandson." He's fifteen. What do you say?
Day one at the coworking space. The only free seats: one by the restroom door, or a window desk at double the price. The budget is counted to the cent. Where do you sit?
The outsourced accountant writes at 8:00: "You need a business account, a tax scheme and twelve signed documents. Today." Shall we?
A designer friend drew a free logo: a purple hedgehog holding a light bulb. You hate it, but your friend was glowing when showing it. Accept?
Gosha wants to build in a trendy new programming language: "It'll be fast and beautiful." Hiring for it will be nearly impossible. Allow it?
At home they ask when you last ate a meal not hunched over a laptop. You honestly can't remember. Close the laptop for the evening?
You open the spreadsheet of personal savings and divide by monthly costs. Seven months. Recalculate optimistically?
You decided to validate the idea this morning by cold-calling twenty potential customers. Three already said "not interested" before you finished. Keep going?
A well-known accelerator is taking applications. Forty questions, including "describe your team as an animal." Deadline: midnight tonight. Apply?
Gosha wants to keep his day job "a couple more months, just in case." So he'll code at night and reply to you every other time during the day. Agree?
You set yourself a deadline: prototype by Friday. It's Wednesday, 10 p.m., and the prototype is one button that does nothing. Pull an all-nighter?
The print shop delivered your business cards. All five hundred have a typo in your title: "Fonder." Meeting in an hour. Hand them out anyway?
left: Hand them out with a smile

text: Your brother offers to invest his kitchen-renovation savings. Decent money, but if it all collapses, family holidays get awkward. Take it?
Your first test user — your neighbor — clicked the wrong thing, broke everything and said, "So convenient!" Log it as a win?
You returned your corporate laptop, and your personal one boots on the third try and smells like an iron. A new one costs a month's living expenses. Buy?
Gosha strolls into the coworking at 11:00: "I'm a night owl." You've been here since eight, and the morning call happened without him. Talk schedules?
A lawyer you know drafted your bylaws for free but wants "a tiny stake" as thanks. He won't say how tiny. What do you do?
You mapped the whole product on a coworking wall with sticky notes. The manager says, "That's not your wall." There are two hundred of them. Take them down?
Former coworkers invite you out Friday "like old times." You miss them, but Friday night was reserved for the business plan. Go?
You promised yourself morning runs because "founders need energy." It's raining, and there's a call at 9:00. Run?
A marketer friend says to start a founder's blog and post daily about the road to success. So far the road is debts and queues. Start?
Gosha demos version one: it works, but the Buy button hides under "Other." "It's more minimalist," he says. Argue?
left: Move the button front and center

text: During a call with a prospect, your cat walked across the keyboard and sent "zzzzxxxx" to the work chat. Explain yourself?
You started a company expense sheet this morning. Line one is "motivational cookies," and it's already the biggest item. Cut it?
A mentor tells you: "Nobody needs your idea. But I like you." Is that a compliment or a death sentence? How do you react?
A prospect will pay if you add a feature nobody planned and only they need. The money is real. Build it?
1 a.m. A new feature idea is spinning in your head, and there's a meeting in the morning. Get up and write it down, or try to sleep?
left: Get up and write it all

text: 47 emails from services you signed up to "try for free." Every trial ended yesterday. Unsubscribe?
Gosha wants your titles to be "Chief Code Wizard" and "Supreme Visionary." You're the visionary. The cards can still be reprinted. Agree?
A courier drops off the standing desk you ordered. It's the size of an ironing board. Returns are at your expense. Keep it?
At home, someone proposes a startup-free weekend. You already have three decks ready for your loved ones. Accept the rule?
In the evening you find a company doing exactly your idea — for three years now, with forty employees. Sleep after that?
You launched a survey for future customers. By morning: 12 replies, nine of them from relatives. Does that count as market research?
Your coworking neighbors are on speakerphone right by your desk. You have a customer interview in ten minutes. Ask them to quiet down?
right: Take the call in the elevator

text: Gosha proposes a proper founders' agreement: who does what, and what happens if you fall out. He keeps making divorce jokes about it. Sign?
The bank turned down a business loan: "Your company is three weeks old." The manager suggests a personal loan instead. Risk it?
A former colleague heard about your startup and wants in. He's great, but you can't pay him a salary for six months. Invite him?
Morning rehearsal in the mirror: the 30-second startup pitch. It runs four minutes, mostly the word "basically." Keep practicing?
You and Gosha argue over who talks to customers. He says you're the talker; you say he knows the product. Decide now.
Tomorrow's to-do list: 31 items. Item 17: "rest." Item 31: "change the world." Trim it?
right: Do it all, whatever it takes

text: To save money you bring coffee from home in a thermos. It leaked all over the printed business plan in your backpack. Meeting at ten. Reprint?
right: Bring it, coffee stains and all

text: Your old school group chat is discussing your news: "Quit a normal job? Bold." Someone asks what exactly you do now. Explain?
The alarm goes off at 6:00 labeled "Real founders are up already." You wrote that yesterday in a burst of motivation. Today it's infuriating. Get up?
Angel investor Vera wants a five-year financial model by lunch. You have a five-week model, on a napkin. What do you send?
Timur, your first hired developer, asks on day one where the docs are. There are none — just Gosha and his memory. What do you say?
left: Sit down and write a wiki

text: You introduced 9:00 stand-ups. Today only you and the cat showed up. Everyone else is "already working." Scrap the ritual?
Rush hour on the subway, and a brilliant landing page idea hits. Your hands are full of handrail and a stranger's backpack. Dictate it out loud?
Gosha wants to rewrite the whole backend: "Past me wrote that code, and past me was an idiot." The code is a month old. Allow it?
left: Give him a week to refactor

text: Designer Liza brings three UI options. All three are gray. "It's minimalism," she explains. Customers say they can't find the buttons.
The team's lunch budget is buckwheat from a shared pot. Timur timidly asks if pizza will ever happen. Answer?
A pilot client wants you to demo the product to their director tomorrow. Currently it can only log in and log out. Agree?
For the first time you calculate what one user costs to acquire. It's more than they'll ever bring in. Show the team?
A basement owner will rent you an office cheap. No windows, but there's a pipe that sometimes sings. The team works from your home for now. Rent it?
In the angel meeting, Gosha said the product is "almost done." It's maybe 20% done. The angel nods happily. Correct him?
left: Correct him in front of her

text: Your very first support ticket: "How do I delete my account?" No other tickets yet. Try to talk them into staying?
11:40 p.m. Gosha sends a nine-minute voice message about how you underrate his contribution. You pitch in the morning. Listen now?
The fridge contains ketchup, half a stick of butter and an energy drink. Walk to the store, or order delivery with this week's last money?
Timur has stayed late three evenings in a row without asking for overtime. You can see he's exhausted. Send him home?
right: Thank him and let him stay

text: Friends invited you to a birthday party. You promised to come, but tonight's release broke and nobody else can fix it. What do you pick?
An evening email from a big company: "Interesting, let's talk." Signed: "Procurement intern." Celebrate?
First time in a week you're in bed before midnight — then you remember the domain expires at 00:00. Get up?
right: Let it drop, fix it tomorrow

text: An accelerator offers money for 7% of the company — plus a mandatory three-month move to another city. Think about it?
Liza shows up with news: she's also working for another startup on the side. "But I love you more!" How do you react?
Your gym membership, bought back in corporate life, expires in a week. You've been once. Go today at 7 a.m.?
Gosha arrives early and announces from the doorway: "I think we need a blockchain." You're building a hair salon booking app. React how?
First review in this morning: "Used it for a week, understood nothing, five stars for courage." Put it on the website?
right: Call and ask what was unclear

text: Timur found a bug that stored all passwords in plain text. He's fixed it. Tell the users? There are forty-one.
Vera will invest, but wants to call you every Friday at 6 p.m. "to chat about life." Good deal. Accept the condition?
A customer calls for the fifth time asking for "the person in charge." That's you, and you've spoken three times already. Pick up?
You're invited to a hackathon: 48 sleepless hours, and the prize is a free office for a month. The team loves it; you love sleep. In?
The basement pipe starts singing — mid video call with an investor. She asks if you're in a sauna.
You could apply for a young-company grant. It takes 60 pages of documents and an illustrated business plan. Slim odds. Apply?
First TV show you've put on in a month. Five minutes in, the hero founds a startup and loses everything. Finish it?
Liza texts tonight: a big company offered her three times the salary. She asks what you think. Honestly?
left: Let her go with your blessing

text: Tonight you notice 140 items marked "urgent." You have more urgency than people and hours. Re-sort them?
right: Delete everything older than a month

text: Your neighbor drills through the wall every evening from 7 p.m., right when you work from home. Knock on the door?
Gosha texts tonight: "What if we quit everything and become bakers?" Clearly he's had a rough day. Reply?
right: Joke it off and go to bed

text: You promised your angel a monthly update. It's the 30th, the report is blank, and the numbers went down. Write it honestly?
Someone pitches you "Founder in 30 Days." It costs a month of rent and promises "billionaire mindset." Sign up?
No power in the basement this morning. Laptops at 40%. The team looks at you like you're the chief electrician. What now?
left: Move to a café for the day

text: Timur is an hour late — overslept after a night fix you asked him to make. Say something?
Your first user newsletter is ready. Just before sending, Gosha spots the subject line: "Dear usres." 900 recipients.
A neighboring startup offers to share the office, coffee machine and cleaner. Their founder talks very loudly on the phone. Team up?
Time to price the product. Gosha wants free "for growth," your angel wants it pricey "for revenue." You cast the deciding vote.
A popular blogger will feature you if you build him a custom feature for free. Huge reach. Deal?
One office chair wobbles and squeaks. Today Timur's on it, tomorrow the new intern. Buy a new one with your own money?
Family dinner. Your nephew asks what you do. You spend three minutes explaining the word "platform." He's asleep. Keep explaining to the adults?
Tonight Timur and Gosha have spent forty messages arguing over a variable name. Tempers rising. Step in?
Flipping through your notebook tonight, you see "call Grandma," three weeks old. It's 9:30 p.m. Call?
Intern Ksyusha arrives with nine ideas to "make everything better." You've tried eight. The ninth isn't bad. Hear all nine?
right: Ask her to write them up

text: First payday for the team. The account covers exactly two of three salaries. The third is yours. Who gets paid?
The new office has five desks and one outlet. The extension cord looks like an octopus. Every morning is a battle for charging. Fix it?
Your old neighbors gave you their coffee machine. Great coffee, but it roars like a jet taking off during every call. Keep it?
8:30 interview with a marketing candidate. He brought a deck on everything you're doing wrong. Thirty slides.
You started scootering to work to save money. Today it's slush outside, and you're meeting a client in light-colored trousers.
New developer Arseny asks when the workday starts. You realize you've never decided. Your answer?
A big corporation emails this morning wanting to buy you "whole" for peanuts. They don't even like you — they want Timur.
Three hours till the fund meeting. Slide seven still says "something smart goes here." What do we do?
Gosha has an idea: "Let's do a four-day week. We're a startup, we're modern." You have three months of cash.
You made a list of a hundred funds. Each deserves a personal email. This morning you managed two. How to speed up?
It's Saturday, but the alarm says "call with fund." They're in another time zone where it's still Friday. Get up?
left: Get up and take the call

text: At 9:00 Ksyusha asks if she can run the company's social media. No experience, oceans of enthusiasm. Trust her?
Café coffee costs as much as lunch. You did the math: a month's salary per year. Switch to instant?
The fund partner stares at his phone the whole meeting. Asked "Are you interested?" he says, "Go on." What now?
Arseny asks when he'll get promoted. He's been here two weeks. You don't want to crush his spirit. Answer?
The accountant says you missed a filing. The fine is small but painful, and must come out of today's ad budget.
A user asks for dark mode. That's request number 57. Gosha says dark mode is "for the weak." Build it?
Tonight Gosha admits he's bored: "We're doing the same stuff as in corporate, only poorer." His eyes look sad.
10 p.m.: the banking app shows a negative balance. The angel's money arrives "any day now." Office rent is due tomorrow.
You're rehearsing the pitch at home. Your partner yawns at minute two — it's their ninth time hearing it. Keep going?
At 11 p.m. Ksyusha posts a meme about your product in the team chat. Funny, slightly hurtful. Everyone's reacting. Respond?
right: Ask her to tone it down

text: Friday, 6 p.m. — Vera calls "to chat about life." Forty minutes in, twenty were about her country house.
A small business podcast invites you on. Recording at 9 p.m.; about 300 listeners, half of them the host's mom.
Tonight your laptop hints the disk is 99% full. It holds three versions of the product, all named "final." Clean up?
8 p.m., update ready to ship. Timur says, "Friday night. Don't." Gosha says, "Do it."
You dream an investor asks for revenue and you answer in code. You wake at 3:40 a.m. Work or sleep?
Your oldest friend invites you camping for the weekend: "Lately all you talk about is the startup." He's right. Go?
Tonight you realize every expense lives in your phone's notes app. The accountant wants a spreadsheet by morning.
Timur texts tonight: "Can I work from home tomorrow? Nothing urgent." There's no remote policy yet.
left: Allow it and write a policy

text: Your partner made dinner and asks for one phone-free hour. Right now the investor has "a couple of questions."
Tonight a user writes a long email: your product helped them open their own salon. You nearly cry. Reply?
Ksyusha posted on the company account with a typo in the product name. It already has more views than every previous post.
The app freezes during the fund demo. Timur whispers, "Restart it." The partner checks the time.
Startups get free conference spots if they staff a booth for eight hours. The booth is a table and a sign.
Gosha proposes firing a difficult client. The client brings a third of revenue — and calls ten times a day.
You overslept for the first time in six months. Everyone's in, and there's a note on the door: "Where's our founder?" Walk in casually?
A design candidate arrives with a cat in a carrier: "No one to leave him with." The cat is calm. Do the interview?
82 unread in the chat this morning. Half of them about who ate someone's yogurt. Read it all?
You cracked a joke on the morning call. Silence. A minute later Gosha DMs: "Haha, got it." Lighten the mood?
You're on a train to meet a fund in another city. It's an hour late. Meeting at 11. What do you do?
right: Join by phone from the train

text: The founder of a rival startup invites you to lunch: "Let's be friends." Is he fishing for info, or does he mean it?
Someone brought a stray kitten into the office. Everyone's working slower, but smiling. Keep it?
Gosha suggests you both take the same week off. "The team will manage." The team is three people and a kitten.
The cloud bill arrives — triple last month's. Someone left a test environment running for a month.
right: Just shut it off and pay

text: The coworking is hosting investor speed-dating: three minutes each. You're twentieth in line.
A one-star review appears: "Doesn't work." An hour later the same person writes: "Sorry, wrong app." The star stays.
There's no meeting room. Important calls happen in the supply closet next to the mops. A client asks about the echo.
Tomorrow is the accelerator's Demo Day: five minutes on stage before a hundred investors. Your revenue slide is terrifyingly honest. Dress it up?
Demo Day dress rehearsal. The host says you talk too fast, and the clicker works every other time. Rehearse till midnight?
Tonight Gosha draws a new arrow on the whiteboard: "What if it's not for hairdressers but for vets?" The arrow looks convincing.
Everyone's gone; you're alone in the office. You could work in peace — or actually go home while it's light out. Which?
Ten users write in at once tonight: "Nothing loads." Timur's at the movies, Gosha is offline. Fix it yourself?
10:15 p.m. The server is down. While it reboots you stare into space and realize you haven't eaten since morning. What first?
Mom asks tonight if it's time to "find a normal job before it's too late." Three hours ago you signed your first big contract. Tell her?
You stayed late and the office kettle died. All that's left is an "energy tea" bag from old neighbors. Drink it at night?
Gosha admits tonight that he sold his car to put money into the company. You're touched and terrified at once. What do you say?
right: Ask him never to do that again

text: Users in the community chat have argued for three hours about whether the product needs a calendar. They want you to settle it.
Tonight you finally calculate how many months the money will last: 4.5. The word "runway" echoes in your head. How do you sleep with that?
Your partner asks when you last had a vacation. That was a past life, back in corporate.
Ksyusha asks tonight if it's normal that she's crying after a client call. He yelled at her for twenty minutes.
Your Demo Day pitch is over. There was applause. Nobody took a card. The host whispers: "Not bad. Bit boring."
Dinner is chips at the monitor, and you catch yourself talking out loud to the code. Warning sign?
A courier shows up tonight with a huge box of logo T-shirts. You didn't order them. Gosha did — with the entire marketing budget.
left: Hand them out with a smile

text: In the feed tonight: a rival just raised a big round. Nobody mentions you in the comments. Close the app?
Just as you lie down: "New sign-up." User number 87! Get up and greet them?
Liza and Arseny haven't spoken since lunch: he called her mockup "a nice picture for a museum." Shared sprint tomorrow.
Your mentor from the old company writes tonight: "Heard you took the leap. Proud of you." You want to unload everything on him.
A mug of tea tipped onto your laptop tonight. It works, but the letter A types "aaa." Live with it till payday?
The fund replies this morning: "Interesting, but too early. Come back with revenue." That's response number fourteen.
left: Reply and add to the plan

text: Arseny arrives in pajama pants: "Hey, it's a startup." A client is visiting today.
The stand-up reveals Gosha and Timur spent a week on the same task. Each did it his own way.
Liza proposes a "quiet hour" from 10 to 11 — no calls, no chat. That's exactly when clients write.
A client sets a meeting for 7:00 a.m., "while the kids are asleep." You are not a morning person. Fake it or say so?
Ksyusha asks in the morning how much money the company has. The whole team freezes, waiting.
You started jogging with Gosha to talk strategy. He runs faster and strategizes alone.
A bill arrives this morning for services you don't remember. One is called "Cloud for Clouds." Pay it?
The landlord warns you this morning: facade repairs this summer, a week of noise. The team doesn't know yet.
The accelerator mentor wants "your North Star" by lunch. You're not sure what that is, but it sounds important.
left: Look it up and invent one

text: Timur mentions this morning that a bank offered him a job. He's not leaving — "just so you know."
A fund will invest — if you replace your co-founder with an "experienced CTO." Gosha is sitting right next to you.
You skipped lunch again. Timur silently puts a sandwich on your desk. You feel awkward. React how?
A client wants 40% off "because we're a startup, you're a startup, we should help each other."
Gosha finds out you met a fund without him. He's hurt: "We're partners." It was a spontaneous meeting.
A small outlet wants an interview: "How did you survive your first failure?" You're not sure you have yet.
The cleaner stopped coming — she wasn't paid. The office is drowning in pizza boxes. Who cleans?
At Demo Day an investor sits beside you: "This season I'm only looking at vet tech." You build for hairdressers.
The tax office sends a letter asking about expenses for "motivational cookies." You need to explain in official language.
right: Call and laugh it off together

text: Arseny wants a second monitor: "My productivity will double." There's money for exactly one monitor for the whole team.
A big platform offers to embed your product. That means rewriting half your code in two weeks.
Ksyusha asks for the day off — it's her birthday. Today is also the launch of the ad campaign she prepared.
right: Ask her to stay till lunch

text: You moved out of town to save on rent. Now it's ninety minutes by train to the office. Work on the ride or sleep?
Timur proposes writing automated tests. That's a week of work and zero new features. Customers are waiting.
This morning you learn the sign-up form has been broken for a week. Nobody knows how many people bounced.
At 7:30 Vera sends an article, "10 Founder Mistakes," captioned: "Recognize yourself?" You recognize yourself in nine.
You downloaded a sleep app that says bedtime is 10:30 p.m. It's 10:25, and your pitch deck isn't finished.
Late tonight you and Gosha talk about something other than work for the first time in a month. Turns out he can't sleep either. Keep talking?
At 9 p.m. you find a chocolate bar in your drawer, saved "for the day everything goes wrong." Today is so-so. Eat it?
right: Save it for a truly bad day

text: You posted a sales job. Overnight: 300 applications, 280 of them a boilerplate "Hello, I am responsible." Read them all?
New salesperson Marina asks on day one where the sales script is. The script is you and your charisma.
You wake at 5:50 thinking, "What if it's all for nothing?" The alarm is an hour away. What do you do with that thought?
A bank wants a pilot, but security sent a 200-question form. Question one: "Describe your data center." You don't have one.
Liza brings a new logo: "The hedgehog is outdated." The hedgehog is on the T-shirts, the mugs and the sign.
A developer candidate asks for more than you and Gosha earn combined. He really is very good.
The office kitten chewed through the router cable overnight. Only someone with a phone hotspot has internet. That's you.
Vera asks you to speak at her breakfast for other angels "as an example." An example of what, she doesn't say.
This morning your eye is twitching — third day running. Gosha says it's "founder eye" and everybody gets it.
You found a bigger office — with a window, a meeting room and a closet. Double the rent, and you're still five people.
The pilot client writes this morning: "We like it so far, but let's change everything." The pilot ends Friday.
Monday. You walk in and Gosha is asleep on the couch hugging his laptop. A note beside him: "Almost fixed it."
You're invited to speak at a big industry conference — for a fee. "The stage isn't free, you know."
You discover Marina tracks clients in her own private spreadsheet. "It's easier for me."
left: Move everything to a shared system
right: Let her do it her way

text: Gosha proposes going "flat": no managers, everyone decides everything together. Yesterday's coffee decision took an hour.
You realize you can't remember what day it is. The calendar says Saturday. You're in the office. Alone.
You accidentally sent the newsletter to all users at 6 a.m. Three have already replied that you woke them up.
A rival just launched the feature you described at Demo Day. Word for word, same joke and all.
Marina closed her first deal and wants the promised bonus now. Gosha promised it. You had no idea.
right: Ask her to wait a month

text: The fund's lawyer sends a term sheet with "liquidation preference" eleven times. You only know the word "liquidation."
Timur admits he's burnt out and wants two weeks off. Without him, the release won't ship.
right: Ask him to wait till after release

text: A user begs for the old design: "The new one is pretty, but I can't find the booking button." Twenty such emails.
Three calls back to back at lunch. Lunch is a banana. Arseny suggests eating together, even for ten minutes.
Your mentor says to "sell the dream," not the numbers. Your dream is hairdressers getting home on time.
Gosha and Marina are fighting: she promises clients features that don't exist; he refuses to build them. Both look at you.
The grant reply: rejected. Reason: "Innovative potential not demonstrated." You demonstrated it over sixty pages.
The office AC died. It's 31°C. The team is in shorts, fanning themselves with pizza boxes. Send everyone home to work?
Marina suggests doubling the price: "Then clients will think we're serious."
Someone eats fish for lunch in the office every day. Anonymous complaints land in your DMs. Ksyusha suspects Arseny.
right: Stay out of the fish affair

text: The fund wants reference calls with your customers. Your happiest customer is Vera — but she's an investor.
Arseny added a new library, and the app is now five times bigger. But "the architecture is beautiful."
At lunch Gosha publicly calls your marketing idea "kindergarten" in the chat. The team goes quiet.
Ksyusha asks to move from marketing into product. Marketing will stall without her.
right: Ask her to find a replacement

text: You update the sheet: four months of cash. Cut marketing and it's six. Cut your own salary too and it's seven.
At home: "You said 'metrics' three times at dinner." Dinner lasted twenty minutes. Switch off work mode?
First phone-free walk in a month. You return to 34 notifications. Nothing caught fire.
The server's down again tonight. Timur's on vacation, Gosha's fixing it, and you're holding his coffee. Help or get out of the way?
right: Go to bed, stay out of it

text: Tonight a rejection arrives from the fund you were counting on most. Short and polite.
left: Email the next one right away

text: Your sister texts: she's getting married next month and wants you to give a toast. You're not sure you'll find time to buy an outfit.
Timur posts a sunset photo: "Finally on vacation." You feel a pang of envy. Message him about a bug?
Friday, 7 p.m. The team invites you to board games. You promised yourself the fund report.
Gosha sends a photo tonight from the pool: "You rest too!" You're answering his work emails at that very moment.
At 11 p.m. you almost buy a course: "Stop Burning Out in 7 Days." It costs a week of Arseny's salary.
A client calls at 10 p.m.: "This button is the wrong shade of blue." You're on the couch, in pajamas.
Liza sends six icon options tonight and wants a pick by morning. They differ by one pixel.
Grandma calls and asks if you need money "for the business." She's been saving from her pension.
right: Take a little, for peace of mind

text: The fund report is almost done. One field left: "Key lesson of the month." The honest answer: "Don't promise clients what doesn't exist."
At night in the kitchen you're debating with yourself whether to carry on. Your partner comes in for water and asks who you're talking to.
A term sheet lands this morning. The valuation is lower than you dreamed, higher than you feared. A week to respond. Negotiate?
Gosha saw the term sheet: "I don't want anyone telling us what to do." Without the money there'll be nobody left to tell in three months.
Timur is back from vacation, tanned and calm. An hour later he opens his email and the calm evaporates. Give him a day to ease in?
Three labels on today's alarms: "Fund," "Payroll," "Dentist." The dentist can be moved. Move it?
The barista by the office knows your order and asks, "How's the startup?" For once this week you can say "good."
New developer Danya starts today. No desk — it's ordered but not delivered. Where does he sit?
The podcast with your interview drops this morning. Listening back, you count forty "like"s. Share the link?
A downpour soaks you through, and a video call with the fund is in thirty minutes. The only spare clothes at the office: a hedgehog T-shirt.
right: Blow-dry your shirt with Liza's hairdryer

text: Arseny posts a long message in the team chat: our processes are "broken." Half the team adds a thumbs up.
Your very first client, a hairdresser, calls at 8:00: "Everything works, just wanted to say thanks." She hangs up.
left: Log it in your wins diary

text: Vera hears about the term sheet and is jealous: "What about me? I found you first." Time to talk.
The elevator is stuck between floors. Inside with you: the fund partner on his way to your meeting. Twenty minutes, probably.
Marina's report: sales up 30%. In tiny print at the bottom: "including promised." Celebrate?
A neighbor learned you have a startup and pitches you his idea at the elevator every morning. Today: an app for finding lost socks.
On day one Danya deployed straight to production. The site works — but now it's purple.
Traffic jam. You're late for your own morning meeting. Forty minutes in the car. Run it from the car?
The coffee machine is out of beans. The team stands around it, staring at you. Nearest shop: twenty minutes away.
The fund's lawyer wants a drag-along clause: if investors sell, you have to sell too. Sounds like a leash.
Gosha says: "Let's skip the VC money and grow on revenue." Revenue covers coffee and half the rent.
The team wants to celebrate a thousand users. The party budget: two pizzas for seven people.
left: Chip in from your own pocket

text: After the pilot, the bank will buy — but pays 120 days after signing. You can't last that long.
Liza asks for a raise: "I do all the design, all the marketing, and I water the plants." There's no money for raises.
Ksyusha drafted a launch press release: "revolution," "breakthrough," "first in history." You just added a calendar.
You've been on your feet all day. Your body begs for twenty minutes on the office couch. Client call in half an hour.
Marina confesses she sold a client a year's subscription to a feature that doesn't exist. They've already paid.
The site crashes during your customer open house. Guests sip tea and stare at "Error 500."
left: Turn it into a backstage tour

text: The fund wants your 18-month plan. You have one; it ends with "and then we take off."
Arseny and Danya are fighting about tabs versus spaces. Hour four, now in the team chat. Clients are waiting.
The fund partner suggests an "informal" lunch with founders of another of his startups. They do almost what you do.
The kitten you kept has grown into a cheeky cat. He's sitting on Timur's keyboard and won't budge.
A user review: "Great, but support only answers at night." Support at night is you.
First lunch alone with Gosha in a month. He says: "I'm not sure I want to keep going." The silence stretches.
New QA tester Polina found 64 bugs on her first day. The team regards her with horror and respect.
Half your costs are foreign services. The exchange rate just jumped. Drop some of them?
You ran an anonymous team survey. Average satisfaction: 6/10. Comments: "more windows."
Tonight you're told: "You've started talking about conversion rates in your sleep." Not sure that's good news.
Danya stayed late to fix the purple site. He apologizes in the chat every ten minutes.
left: Send him home with a smile

text: The fund partner invites you to dinner at a fancy restaurant — splitting the bill. Your share equals the company's daily budget.
10 p.m. Gosha texts: "Thought it over. I'm staying. But I want us to talk more." You can't handle a long talk tonight.
You signed up for evening boxing to blow off steam. Tonight the coach pairs you with another startup founder.
11 p.m. A client writes: "Urgent! Need the report by 9 a.m." The product generates it automatically, but the button is well hidden.
Tonight you tally the team's stock options and realize you promised more than 100% of the company. Total: 104%.
Midnight, eating cold buckwheat from the pot. Your partner comes in and sits beside you silently. Talk?
Polina sends tomorrow's bug list tonight. It's longer than the feature list. Rethink the release?
Someone sends you a video: a famous entrepreneur recommends "four hours of sleep." Comments are ecstatic. You doze off at minute three.
The team gives you a mug tonight: "World's Best Founder (out of one)." Laugh or cry?
Marina calls tonight: the client will sign if you personally come at 8 a.m. tomorrow, across town.
You fell asleep on the office couch. At 2 a.m. the security guard wakes you: "Building's closing." Go home?
A friend's therapist suggested a gratitude journal. Tonight's entry: "Grateful the server only crashed once."
Tomorrow is the big launch. Everything's ready but one little thing: nobody tested payments. It's 9 p.m.
The guard does his 10:30 p.m. rounds and peeks in: "You again? Do they even pay you?" Answer honestly?
A journalist sends the interview for approval tonight. Your quote: "We'll destroy the market." You said "change."
After launch Gosha proposes three days off for everyone. Support tickets are pouring in like never before.
You've spent the evening refreshing the sign-up counter every 10 seconds. The number barely moves.
left: Close it, go for a walk

text: A friend invites you to a movie "with zero business in it." Your chance to breathe. But the fund meeting is tomorrow.
Tonight a huge bouquet arrives "for the founder, from a grateful client." No card. The team is spinning theories.
Launch! Three hours in: two hundred sign-ups and one complaint: "Too cheerful." Celebrate with the team?
Danya admits tonight he's scared to talk on calls, so he stays silent. You've only heard his ideas in chat.
left: Let him write ideas in advance

text: Your mentor Oleg calls tonight: "You're not a founder, you're a firefighter. You put out every fire yourself." He's not wrong.
Your nephew sends a video: he explains your product to his class and gets an A. You're touched.
A client in another time zone calls at midnight — noon for him. Urgent billing question.
Tonight you delegated ten of your tasks to Timur for the first time. An hour later he returns three marked "don't get it."
Polina finds a bug tonight that could ruin the launch. Fixing it will take all night.
right: Send her home, take the risk

text: Tonight you drafted a plan to become a "unicorn" within a year. It might look different in the morning. Show the team now?
Home for dinner for the first time in a week. Everyone's surprised. The dog barks at you like a stranger.
Tonight's report: new users log in, click "Hello" and leave forever. 70% of them.
A salon owner writes a thank-you at 11 p.m. and asks for a "friendship discount" next year.
The courier brings your weekly groceries tonight — you forgot to answer the door. He's been waiting fifteen minutes.
Morning headline: a big corporation launches a free clone of your product. The team is already in the chat.
Vera sends an article about the competitor this morning: "Is this the end for you?" Half the morning ruined.
Timur this morning: "A corporation copied us? Means there's a market." He's smiling. You feel lighter.
left: Make it the motto of the day

text: You called clients after the corporation news. Nine out of ten: "We're staying — your support is human."
left: Use the quotes on the site

text: First thing, Arseny suggests "copying the best parts from the corporation." The corporation copied the best parts from you.
You start the day with a workout video. The trainer is suspiciously chipper for 6:30 a.m. Keep going?
A marketing candidate sends his test task this morning: a whole campaign with a video. He didn't ask for money.
Gosha arrives at 7:00 — unheard of. "I woke up and realized how we beat the corporation." The plan is on a napkin.
The bank froze the account "pending review." Payday is today. The manager will be in touch "within three days."
left: Go to the branch in person
right: Warn the team about the delay

text: Ksyusha is late for the third time this week. Today she brought cake: "So you won't be mad." Great cake.
Organizers write this morning: a speaker is ill — could you step in, three hours from now? Topic: "The Future of Fintech."
Liza unveils the new landing page this morning. It's gorgeous — and has no price. "Prices scare people off," she says.
On the bus you spot someone using your app. You want to say hi. He looks annoyed.
Choose: spend the remaining budget on ads or on one more salesperson.
The corporation invites you to meet: "Let's discuss a partnership." You suspect they want to swallow you. Go?
Gosha hears about the corporate meeting: "If we sell out, I'm gone." You haven't decided anything.
You take a candidate to lunch and he orders the priciest dish on the menu. Your lunch budget is soup.
A user sends a screen recording. You watch him hunt for one button for twenty minutes.
Danya offers to build a mobile app over the weekend. "I want to, it's a hobby." A weekend hobby?
The fund ordered a financial audit before the deal. The auditor wants the contract for "motivational cookies."
Ksyusha asks to become a "brand ambassador" — meaning she wants to vlog about the office. With the cat.
The lawyer advises trademarking the hedgehog. A month of paperwork and the cost of Timur's salary.
A dance studio opened next door. Lunchtime is salsa. Your calls now have a soundtrack.
Marina brought a client into the office unannounced. You're in a hedgehog T-shirt and slippers.
The corporation's clone crashed under load. Their users are flocking to you. Your server is trembling.
Timur asks to be promoted to tech lead. Gosha objects: "I'm the tech lead." Timur carries half the codebase.
The accountant reports you paid three months of payroll tax for a hire who never showed up. You can get it back — in six months.
Mid-demo, Gosha launches into database architecture. The client owns a flower shop.
A big client requires your staff to complete its internal security course. Eight hours long.
The alarm died; you wake up because the cat sat on your face. It's 9:40. The call was at 9:30.
The fund partner writes this morning: "We're in if you close two more clients by month's end." Nine days left.
Morning A/B results: the green button beats blue by 0.3%. Gosha wants everything green; Liza wants to cry.
Danya asks what stock options are and what they'll be worth "when we're as big as those guys." Honest answer?
In the morning retro, the "what went badly" column has an anonymous note: "The founder decides everything for us." The handwriting looks like Liza's.
The ficus Vera gave you is withering. She's coming by at lunch today. Buy an identical one?
Your first board meeting. You bought a blazer, but everyone in the office wears hoodies. Wear it?
Everyone on the team got an email "from you" this morning: "Urgently wire money to the supplier." Ksyusha already opened the attachment.
Your scooter broke and taxis are pricey. The office is 4 km away. Walking is healthy — and slow.
Ksyusha posts a morning video of the office cat. He has more followers than the company. Make him the brand's face?
The office printer only prints diagonally. You need to sign a contract in triplicate in an hour.
Four hours of sleep. 9:00 big client, 10:00 the fund. Coffee isn't working.
Danya shyly shows off a feature he built "outside his tasks." It's better than what you'd planned.
right: Ask him to do assigned work first

text: Renewal notice for a meditation app. You've opened it once.
Mom calls at 8:00: she read about you in the paper and bought ten copies. "They called you a young founder!"
At the board meeting an investor asks for "Plan B if things go badly." You have Plan A and faith.
Timur proposes a night on-call rota so you stop fixing everything yourself. Each shift earns a day off.
Liza proposes fifteen minutes of yoga for everyone before work. Marina says that's her call time.
Stuck in traffic you invented a whole company pivot. By the time you arrive, you've changed your mind. Tell the team?
Monthly churn: 15%. Gosha says it's "normal for the market." Marina says it's Gosha's fault.
left: Review it with both of them

text: Ksyusha suggests buying a hundred positive reviews: "Everybody does it." It's cheap.
An investor on the board suggests firing half the team to stretch the money. The team is five people.
Everyone eats together at one table. Today's topic: whose laptop fan is loudest. Join them or keep working?
You find that Arseny stored the server passwords in a shared doc called "Misc." Anyone with the link can open it.
The owner of a 30-salon chain wants to buy for every location — at 60% off. That's your annual revenue.
Polina begs not to ship on Friday: "We'll be fixing it all weekend again." Gosha thinks she's being alarmist.
Gosha suggests hiring a "Chief Happiness Officer." You'd rather hire a Chief Revenue anybody.
Five people in the office, all on the phone at once. You can only hear Marina. Buy partitions?
Your mentor asks you to talk to the new accelerator cohort about mistakes. You've got enough for a TV series.
The client has been silent for two full minutes. Marina whispers: "Whoever speaks first loses."
The corporation offers to buy you. Good money — everyone on the team could buy a car. But they'd probably shut the product down.
The office fridge smells odd. Nobody admits the food in there is theirs.
New salesperson Semyon needs a laptop. The only spare is your old one, with the "aaa" key.
The blogger you turned down posts "Why This Startup Is Doomed." The comments are split.
Time for the monthly investor update. Last month was "all good." This month is "all good, but."
Tonight Liza admits she wrote the note about "the founder who decides everything." She's embarrassed. So are you.
On his first evening Semyon stays till nine calling clients. Half of them are hairdressers just off their shifts.
left: Praise him and send him home

text: You dream the logo hedgehog is chairing the board, saying: "Time to rest." You wake at 4 a.m.
On the evening train you run into a former coworker from corporate. She asks: "So, any regrets?"
Gosha sends a link to a seaside apartment tonight: "We'll buy this once we sell?" You haven't decided to sell.
Your dad asks tonight if you need help "with the paperwork." He's a retired accountant and really wants to help.
You recalculate the runway again at night. If the corporation buys you, everyone's set. If not, it lasts till spring.
Ksyusha posts a clip tonight: the cat "chairing a meeting." 50,000 views in an hour. The site is buckling under the traffic.
Friends invite you to dinner on one condition: "Nothing about the startup." You last forty minutes in silence. It's hard.
Reading survey responses tonight. One user writes: "Without you I'd have closed my salon." You want to cry.
left: Print it and pin it up

text: Arseny sends his resignation tonight: he's joining the corporation that's copying you. "Nothing personal."
In the shower you get an idea to double revenue. The notebook is in the other room. All you have is a steamy mirror.
right: Repeat it aloud till you're out

text: The upstairs neighbor flooded your apartment. While you call the emergency line, release questions pour into the chat.
right: Answer the chat holding a bucket

text: Sunday, 8 p.m. Thoughts of Monday are ruining the last hours of the weekend. Prepare in advance?
Polina asks when you last tested the backups. Turns out: never. They're made, but do they restore? A mystery.
A package arrives tonight from a user in another city: a jar of homemade jam and a note, "Thanks for the app."
right: Have it with tea at home

text: Arseny throws a farewell party at a café and invites everyone. Gosha pointedly won't go. And you?
Gosha proposes team building: Saturday, 7 a.m., kayaking. Half the team can't swim; the other half can't wake up.
Polina says Danya has been silent for two days with zero commits. He sits in headphones, staring at nothing.
The corporation's lawyers send a 90-page draft acquisition agreement. Reply due Friday.
right: Pay a lawyer to read it

text: You read that cold morning showers "turn people into founders." It's 6:45, and the water is freezing.
New guy Semyon asks: should he call clients using Marina's script or "his own way"? He has a peculiar style.
You logged 74 hours this week. The time tracker congratulates you on a record and awards a medal.
The building owner offers a bigger space "at the old price." The catch: no heating.
At 7:07 Vera sends a link to her new blog, "Notes of an Angel." The first post is about you, with a basement-era photo.
right: Ask her to remove the photo

text: Polina posted twenty rules on the fridge this morning. Rule 14: "No moping by the microwave."
You let the team pick a no-meetings day. They all pick Friday. Investors only call on Fridays.
Ksyusha suggests a contest: "Best haircut booked through our app." Prizes come out of your pocket.
Liza arrives with an idea: a "nineties-style" app. Users over forty will love it; others probably won't.
9:00 a.m. and you've had three coffees, two fires and one resignation. The day's barely begun.
The bank where you ran the pilot says the project is "frozen due to a leadership change." A month of work down the drain.
left: Push for a meeting with the new boss
right: Let it go and move on

text: Gosha announces a weekend "digital detox." No contact. There's a big release this weekend.
Your office building is starting a tenants' morning choir. The director already put you in the altos.
Your payment processor froze incoming payments: "suspicious activity." The activity is a flood of customers after the viral video.
Danya confesses he's struggling: remote is lonely, the office is loud. He's thinking of quitting.
right: Ask him to take a week

text: At the meeting the corporation explains: they don't want your product, just your clients. The offer stands.
Timur at lunch: "If we sell, I want to be the first to know." Everyone stops chewing.
A user writes: "I booked a haircut through your app and ended up in a different city." Investigate?
Polina found a bug in Gosha's code. Gosha says it's a "feature." Users say it's a bug.
right: Turn the bug into a feature

text: A fire safety inspection arrives at lunch. The octopus extension cord makes the inspector laugh nervously.
You held a strategy session. Two hours in, the whiteboard has a hedgehog, a rocket and "we must do something."
left: Keep going till there's a result

text: Marina asks to join the fund meeting: "I know how to sell." The fund expects the founders.
A major TV channel invites you on live to talk about "young entrepreneurs." The thought alone makes you blush.
Timur proposes open-sourcing part of the product: "The community will help." Investors fear competitors will steal it.
A client complains the app is too "playful" and demands a strict mode for serious salons.
right: Refuse — the hedgehog is who we are

text: You notice you haven't left your chair all day. Legs numb, head buzzing.
Ksyusha suggests hiring another intern "so I have someone to drink tea with." There's no budget.
Danya wants to work a week from his grandmother's village. The internet there "almost exists."
right: Ask him to stay in town

text: A new investor asks you to send him all your passwords "for due diligence." You've never met him.
You're at an entrepreneurs' breakfast. Your tablemate sells coffee franchises and wants your revenue and your phone number.
10:40 p.m. Danya calls: "I've decided to stay. Thanks for not pressuring me." You smile in the dark.
Your sister texts: "You promised to come to the dress fitting." It was today at six. It's nine now.
Release done. Not a single crash. You can't believe it and wait for disaster till midnight.
left: Trust it and go to bed

text: An acquaintance offers you evening consulting at his company. Good money, three evenings a week.
The office cat is alone tonight because everyone went to Polina's birthday. The guard texts a photo: the cat looks sad.
right: Ask the guard to feed him

text: Gosha sends a spreadsheet tonight: "Who did what" over six months. His column is noticeably longer.
For your anniversary you're given a weekend trip. No laptop, "or we don't go."
A user writes tonight: "Why do you look so tired in the video?" You really do.
Timur recommends a show about founders. You see yourself in every episode. Funny or terrifying?
Your nephew needs help with a school project, "My Business." He picked your startup and wants an interview.
Semyon sends a list tonight: 40 clients ready for calls. They all want the founder.
Someone posts tonight: "This startup runs on one person." Flattering and terrifying at once.
Arseny writes tonight from the corporation: "It's boring here. Can I come back?" It's been two weeks.
Midnight hunger. The fridge holds one yogurt labeled "DO NOT TOUCH! Timur."
A magazine needs a founders' portrait. The photographer wants "winners": arms crossed, gazing into the distance. Gosha giggles.
right: Shoot a silly one with the cat

text: Five people ahead of you at the pharmacy tonight. An investor calls. Step out and lose your place?
Tonight you tally the month: revenue up, the team tired, you even more so. Announce a break?
The round's money landed this morning. You've never seen that many zeros. The team awaits a speech.
Gosha's morning list of post-round purchases: laptops, chairs, a hammock and a projector. Total: a quarter of the round.
After the round you need five hires in a month. You've never hired five people in a year.
For the first time in six months you wake up without anxiety. Strange feeling. Forgot something?
A realtor shows you the dream office: panoramic windows, a kitchen, meeting rooms. Rent would eat a third of the round in a year.
The fund partner writes: "Congrats! Expect weekly reports, Mondays by 9 a.m." Mondays will never be the same.
Timur asks this morning if raises are coming. You promised "after the round." The round was yesterday.
right: Ask for a month to crunch numbers

text: The new recruiter sends 40 résumés on day one. Every candidate is a self-described "rock star."
right: Ask for a shortlist of five

text: Vera calls to congratulate you and immediately asks you to find her niece "some position."
No alarm needed: a 5:30 a.m. notification about a big new client woke you. No going back to sleep now.
Ksyusha wants a real title instead of "intern." She suggests "Head of Cat Relations."
right: Keep her an intern till fall

text: The board wants a three-year strategy by Friday. You don't know what's happening next week.
Danya says he's figured out how to make the app three times faster. He needs a month and no interruptions.
The new laptops arrived. Everyone wants the old ones "for the kids." Four laptops, eight people.
Timur and Polina invite you on a morning run in the park. You haven't run in six months, but you want to fit in.
Polina hands in her notice: a big company offered her double the pay to test their software.
Gosha wants to name the new meeting room "Launchpad." Liza wants "Chill Room." You want the argument to end.
A product manager candidate asks, "What's your culture like?" You realize you don't know.
You can finally pay for lunches. Gosha wants catering; the team wants cash.
New hire Gleb called the original team "self-taught amateurs" on an all-hands call. Timur switched off his camera.
After the update, users complain the logo hedgehog looks "angry." Liza says he looks "determined."
The board wants an annual budget broken down by month. You build spreadsheets while the product stands still.
Gleb, a veteran from corporate, wants code review for every single line. The old-timers are revolting.
Over lunch, the fund partner casually asks: "Why haven't you hired a CFO yet?"
For the first time all year, Gosha arrives at a meeting with a prepared deck. You're stunned. Slide five: his vacation.
right: Ask him to wait a month

text: The cat climbed into a box of new laptops and won't come out. Gleb demands "the animal be removed from the office."
right: Build the cat his own corner

text: You've been nominated for "Startup of the Year." Fill in a form and shoot a video in three days.
The accountant notices someone bought a gaming subscription on the company card. Gosha's card.
A great candidate wants to work remotely from a far-off time zone. Meetings would have to be at 7 a.m.
An investor advises renaming: "A hedgehog isn't serious." Thousands of users already recognize the logo.
Timur and Gleb are fighting about architecture. Gleb: "Big companies don't do it this way." Timur: "We're not a big company."
First full-hour lunch in a year. Your phone buzzes in your pocket. Look?
The night after closing the round you sit at home and feel no joy. Just exhaustion. Is that normal?
Your partner suggests celebrating the round at a restaurant, just the two of you. You're so tired you just want to lie down.
Gleb sends a 12-page doc tonight: "How We Stop Being a Startup." Subtitle: "and Become a Company."
The team chat debates a retreat: sea, mountains or "just sleep." "Just sleep" is winning.
Polina sends a farewell email to everyone. Last line: "Test your Friday releases." The team is sad.
You open the codebase for the first time in a month and don't recognize it: Gleb rewrote everything. It's better. You're sad.
right: Ask him to explain every line

text: Grandma congratulates you on the round and asks if she's getting her money back with interest. You did borrow a little.
Lying in bed: what if the round runs out and there's no growth? Last year's fear, back again.
left: Write it down and let go
right: Get up and redo the model

text: An old friend invites you fishing this weekend: "You're rich now, relax." You're not rich — the company has money.
Sunday night. The first weekly fund report is due at 9 a.m. No template.
The office empties out. You look at eight desks and remember how it all began at the kitchen table. Snap a photo?
Gosha tonight: "You know, it used to be more fun." You know what he means, but you can't go back.
right: Say this is how it should be

text: A CFO candidate will only meet at 9 p.m., after their day job.
You want to give the team a keepsake from the round. Options: hedgehog mugs or an extra day off.
At 9 p.m. Vera drops by "for a minute" with a cake. The minute lasts two hours.
Gleb sends you a list of 30 "tech debts" tonight. Every one marked "critical."
You're asked to mentor at the accelerator you once went through. Two hours a week and a heap of other people's ideas.
Gleb proposes daily written work reports. The team mutters about "corporate creeping in."
New CFO Alla asks on her first day why the expenses include "hammock (strategic)."
Monday, 8:55. The fund report isn't out because Gleb spent Sunday "improving" the template. It's broken.
Gosha wants to launch a second product — for barbershops. "Basically the same thing, but with beards."
Only you and the cat came into the new office. Everyone else is "working from home, traffic." Every Tuesday.
New product manager Kirill proposes at 9:00 that you "rethink the vision." You explained it only yesterday.
right: Ask him to settle in for a month

text: The new office has a fabulously expensive coffee machine. It makes twenty kinds of coffee, none of them well.
left: Bring back the old roaring one

text: A big salon chain sends a complaint: the app booked three people into one chair. One of them was their director.
You wake up feeling like you didn't sleep at all. Third week running. Cancel your morning meetings?
Ksyusha reports the company's social account got hacked. It's now selling watches.
right: Joke about the watches from a new account

text: You moved closer to the office, but the neighbors renovate from 8 a.m. The drill beats any alarm clock.
Danya demos the sped-up app: three times faster. No user has noticed yet.
Alla says this morning: at the current burn, the money lasts 14 months, not 24.
The founder next door suggests swapping employees "for a day, for a fresh perspective."
Timur admits that for the first time in a year he doesn't want to come in. He's not leaving, just tired.
The stand-up that used to take ten minutes now lasts an hour. More people, fewer decisions.
You dream you're back in corporate and everything is calm. You wake unsure if it was a good dream.
An investor asks at the board: "Why is revenue growing slower than headcount?" Good question.
Kirill proposes a weekly "decisions digest" so nobody misses anything. The first one is nine pages long.
Gosha and Kirill argue over who owns the product. Gosha: "I invented it." Kirill: "I was hired for it."
The team has grown and scatters at lunch. Liza sighs: "We used to eat buckwheat together."
A PR agency pitches a "big news hook": a hedgehog hot-air balloon over the city. It costs six months of Danya's salary.
200 tickets in the queue. Both support staff are off sick. Who answers?
Gleb demands a private office: "You can't think in an open space." The only free room is the mop closet.
A marketing candidate knows everything about promotion but mixes up your name with the rival's. Three times.
The landlord bans hanging anything on the walls. Sticky notes, hedgehogs and the product map are homeless.
Marina found a client who wants you "in a box" on their own servers. It's new work for everyone.
Alla bans company-paid taxis. Gosha takes a taxi to every meeting.
Danya asks: "Are we still a startup?" He liked it when it was five people and a kitten.
left: Spin up a small team for him

text: Mid-afternoon you notice you've read the same email three times without understanding a word.
Ksyusha proposes an evening livestream: "The Founder Answers." Questions come in anonymously.
Arseny, who came back and left again, calls: "Can I get a reference?" He didn't leave gracefully.
At home, the idea of getting a dog comes up: "You need to walk at least twice a day." Sounds like a cunning plan.
11:30 p.m. Kirill emails: "URGENT: strategy." Inside: a poll on button color.
right: Reply now and ask him to stop

text: The team invites you to play table tennis after work. You're terrible but really want to.
Gosha says tonight: "I don't think the company needs me anymore." He has fewer tasks than Kirill now.
Gleb in the chat tonight: "Who broke the build?" You did, when you "quickly fixed a typo."
Tonight you see in the bank statement that you're still paying for the basement you left three months ago.
A friend asks for advice: she wants to leave corporate and found a startup. You see yourself eighteen months ago.
You finally made it to the gym tonight. The trainer asks your goal. Your goal is "survive till Friday."
At night you realize you know only half your employees' names. The company grew without you noticing.
right: Ask Kirill for an org chart

text: The cat no longer sleeps on your lap — he's moved to Gleb's. The first betrayal of the day.
At home you find a box from the first office: the hedgehog sketch, the broken power strip and the receipt for "motivational cookies."
left: Bring it to the new office
right: Toss it — time to move on

text: Your old post "How I Left Corporate" suddenly went viral. Except you didn't write it — Gosha did, in your name.
An elderly hairdresser calls support and asks for "the person who invented it all" to explain. It'll take an hour.
Anonymous survey: "Do you know where the company is headed?" 60% said no. 20% said "headed?"
Liza asks to become head of design and hire two designers under her. Until now she was the only one.
Tonight you record a ten-minute voice note telling Gosha how much you value him. Send it, or is that too much?
You took the laptop to bed "just to check one thing." Two hours ago.
The neighbors' kid drew you with the caption "The person with the hedgehog." It's taped up in the elevator.
The intern you took on in spring writes tonight: "Thanks, I learned a lot. I'm leaving to start my own thing."
Alla's morning report: revenue fell for the first time in a year. Board meeting Thursday.
The board advises cutting three people. You look at the list: you hired each one yourself and remember their first day.
You propose a temporary 20% pay cut for all, so nobody gets fired. You'll announce it at the morning meeting.
Kirill proposes a pivot this morning: "Forget salons — let's do gyms." He has a spreadsheet.
You can't bring yourself to open the laptop. Just sitting with coffee, staring out the window. It's 10:15.
Timur says this morning: "If there are layoffs, cut me — I have savings. Danya has a mortgage."
A morning article: "Has the Star Startup Deflated?" With a photo of you mid-yawn.
Vera calls before the board meeting: "I'm on your side, but the others are angry." That's half-reassuring.
left: Ask for her support at the meeting

text: Danya brings in a fitness-club app prototype. He built it at night, "just in case."
right: Ask him to stop working nights

text: You've started running in the mornings for real. Five kilometers today. Body in shock, mind clear.
Users send a petition: "Don't change anything!" Signed by 1,200 salons.
right: Make the pivot a second product

text: Marina confesses: two big clients are leaving for the corporation. She knew a week ago but was afraid to say.
right: Talk it through calmly with her

text: You suggest moving from the big office back to a small one to save money. The hammock won't fit.
Gleb says the corporation offered him a job, "but I want to see how this ends."
right: Let him go, no hard feelings

text: Ksyusha proposes a charity drive: "Free haircuts for job seekers." Good PR and a good deed.
Alla canceled the office coffee order. The team brings their own. The machine looks sad.
left: Buy coffee with your own money

text: The founder next door says this morning he's shutting down. He's giving away furniture and asks if you need a cat.
At the board meeting, an investor suggests bringing in an "experienced CEO." You'd remain the "visionary founder."
Gosha unexpectedly stands up at the board meeting: "Without this person, there is no company." Everyone looks at you.
Eating alone at a café, you overhear the next table discussing your product: "Not bad, but pricey."
You decided not to cut anyone but to slash all costs. Kirill says that's "delaying the inevitable."
A client who left for the corporation calls: "Their support takes three days. Can we come back?"
Mid-afternoon you shut the meeting room door and just breathe for five minutes. Someone knocks.
Alla finds a saving: cheaper servers. Danya says everything will slow down.
Liza suggests a redesign "to show we're alive." That's a month of work in tough times.
A strong developer writes: "Heard you're struggling. I'll help for equity, no salary."
A journalist asks for comment: "Is it true you're on the brink of closing?" Not true, but nearly.
Gosha suggests you both forgo salaries for a while. He's already squared it with his wife. You need to square it with yourself.
A shampoo maker wants to advertise in your app. You need the money, but ads annoy users.
The team is watching funny startup videos at lunch. One of them is about you. You walk in.
The corporation offers you a job as "division head." Your company would close.
The cat is ill and needs a vet trip. Alla won't allow company money for it.
You ask the team for feedback. You get: "You've become tense."
left: Own it and work on it

text: Tonight the corporation announces it's shutting down its clone of your product. "It didn't take off."
You get home and sink onto the hallway stool. Too tired to take your shoes off. Your partner brings tea right there.
Gosha calls tonight: "Remember the kitchen table? Let's go back and start over?" It's a joke, probably.
Semyon texts tonight: "Closed a one-year deal with a twenty-salon chain." This saves the quarter.
Grandma calls tonight: "Are you eating?" You realize that today you haven't.
You bought "How to Survive a Startup Crisis." Read the foreword and fell asleep.
Danya sends a video tonight: a gym owner loved his fitness prototype and wants to pay.
Someone posts in the team chat tonight: "We'll make it." Everyone hearts it. Even Gleb.
You dream you're at Demo Day, the slides are all photos of the cat, and investors applaud. You wake up smiling.
right: Write it down as an idea

text: Your parents invite you to dinner and promise not to ask about work. Five minutes in, Dad asks about revenue.
Gleb texts tonight: "I've decided to stay. It's more interesting than corporate. Just don't tell anyone I said that."
Walking home, you pass a salon that uses your app. Through the window: a screen with the hedgehog.
You're told: "I think you've forgotten we have a life outside the startup." It stings because it's true.
At 10 p.m. the investor who wanted to replace you with an "experienced CEO" calls: "I was wrong. The numbers are good."
Timur sends a photo tonight: he finally built the wardrobe that sat boxed for six months. "The vacation helped."
Tonight Alla sends the report: profitable for the first time in three months. By about five dollars, but still.
left: Print it and hang it up
right: Find a way to double it

text: The cat recovered. The vet wants a photo for the "Our Patients" wall. In the photo he's wearing a hedgehog T-shirt.
You're flying to an industry expo abroad. Flight at 6:10, taxi at 4:00. Sleep, or don't bother?
right: Stay up and finish the slides

text: At the airport, the box of booth brochures is overweight. The fee equals the cost of the brochures.
right: Hand out half in the queue

text: Your booth sits between the corporation's giant stand and a free ice-cream stand. Nobody comes to you.
left: Hand out the neighbors' ice cream
right: Roam the hall with a tablet

text: Abroad, you wake at 4 a.m. local time. Back home the team is starting work and sending questions.
You need an interpreter for an expo meeting. Gosha says he "knows the language from TV shows."
At the hotel breakfast you're seated across from the founder of a big foreign startup. He eats his omelet, eyes down.
A foreign fund wants all documentation in English by Monday. Two hundred pages.
Ksyusha sends a morning photo: the cat sitting in your chair, "covering" for you. Caption: "He's doing better."
You're invited to a business breakfast where everyone introduces themselves in a foreign language in one minute.
left: Go and give it a shot

text: At the hotel Gosha announces: "Let's open an office here. Better weather." You came for three days.
Danya calls from the office at 7:00 your time: server down, Gleb on vacation. You're abroad with bad Wi-Fi.
A 40-minute morning layover in an unfamiliar airport, terminals at opposite ends. Your backpack holds the laptop with tomorrow's pitch.
right: Give up, take the next flight

text: Your return flight is delayed six hours. You find a quiet airport corner with an outlet.
While you were away, Kirill reorganized: everyone has new titles. Timur is now "Quality Ambassador."
The morning after the expo: 30 emails from foreign prospects. Half in languages you don't know.
The previous guest set the room alarm for 4 a.m. You're wide awake, and the expo doesn't open till ten.
A foreign client wants the app in their language within a month. You have no translators, only an online dictionary.
A man spends half an hour at your booth explaining he doesn't need your product. He leaves with all your brochures.
A partner suggests a business lunch featuring a dish you've never tried. It's moving.
At the expo Gosha befriended every neighboring booth. Now you have ten party invitations.
While you were away, the team rearranged the desks "for better energy flow." Your desk is now by the restroom.
A foreign fund will invest — if the company is registered in their country.
Timur, now "Quality Ambassador," asks what that means. Kirill doesn't know either.
Alla wants the trip expense report. You've lost the receipt for a dinner for ten.
Gleb's back from vacation, having designed a new architecture on the beach. The vacation didn't take.
Your startup made the final of an international competition. It's in a week, in yet another country.
You realize that for a month you haven't had a single day without a flight, call or meeting.
The board suggests entering three new countries at once. You haven't mastered your own yet.
A foreign user writes: "Why a hedgehog? Where I'm from, a hedgehog means rain." Rebrand per country?
A foreign partner presents you with a huge vase. It won't fit in any suitcase.
Marina wants to take the next trip instead of you: "I can talk too." And it's true.
The roaming bill arrives. You called the office an hour a day. The sum is obscene.
Evening at the hotel. Rooftop networking, or room service and a call home?
Video call with home. Your nephew proudly reports he's taught your cat to sit. You miss them.
At the expo party you're introduced to an investor who only talks about golf. You know nothing about golf.
Tonight Gosha admits he's lost his passport. Your flight is at 9 a.m. tomorrow.
left: Go with him to the consulate

text: Packing tonight. Half the space is brochures, a quarter is gifts for the team, the rest is clothes. What goes?
You get home late at night. You're welcomed with a sign: "Welcome home, Founder."
At 11 p.m. a foreign client calls: it's morning for them, a contract question. Your language skills extend to "thank you."
left: Call back tomorrow with an interpreter
right: Muddle through with an online translator

text: You brought the team souvenirs. Magnets for everyone, a snow globe for Gleb. The others eye him suspiciously.
Since returning, you fall asleep at 6 p.m. and wake at 2 a.m. The team writes by day; you reply at night.
Tonight you sum up the trip: three contacts, one potential client and forty cards from people you don't remember.
The board wants a trip report by morning with an "assessment of international potential." Your assessment: "People get haircuts there too."
Your first walk around your neighborhood in a month. Three new cafés opened and you didn't even know.
Liza sends a sketch of the hedgehog in a hat: "For the international version." He looks like a tourist.
You dream you're in an airport and can't find your gate because every screen shows metrics.
right: Wake up and check the metrics

text: At home: "Take me on the next trip. At least for the weekend."
The team relaxed while you were away: at 10:00 two people are in. The rest text "on my way" with photos of their beds.
Semyon asks you to teach him to negotiate with foreign clients. Your own experience: one expo.
You forgot a souvenir for Danya. He doesn't let on, but you notice the sad magnet on his fridge — from Timur.
Your first firing: a new salesperson hasn't closed a deal in three months and is always late. The talk is at 9:30.
Kirill wants sign-off on the "company values" for the website. Draft: "We love hedgehogs and hate Friday releases."
Three new hires start today. Nobody set up their accounts. Timur looks at you: "I did it last time."
You started a five-minute "gratitude round" each morning. Gleb thanks the coffee machine.
New designer Vika asks Liza on day one why the hedgehog is purple. Liza starts explaining from the very beginning.
The team wants three remote days a week. You love the office because everyone's there. The vote: 9 to 1.
Danya asks for a mentor. You'd love to be it, but that takes two hours a week you don't have.
Vika brought in twenty plants "for the vibe." Now Gleb sneezes and the cat eats the leaves.
You came in at 7:30 for some quiet work. Semyon's already there — same idea.
Morning gossip by the door: the company is "about to be acquired." You know nothing about it.
Kirill decreed: official email only, no chats. The team chat went silent for the first time in two years.
A team lead candidate shows up with a reference from Arseny, who left on bad terms.
Liza's off for a month. Without her, nobody knows where the logo source files live.
Polina, who left in spring, writes: "Corporate is boring. Will you take me back?" You've already hired a replacement.
You're stuck in traffic while Kirill runs the morning meeting. You hear him say: "Let's decide this without the founder."
The morning chat debates who eats chips loudest. Turns out it's you.
Gleb proposes rating staff on 47 criteria. Criterion 46: "sense of humor."
Vika and Liza are fighting over a font. It's gotten personal: "Your taste is like a calculator's."
Vera arrives at lunchtime with pies for the whole team. She wants to "chat with the kids."
Time to split the quarterly bonus. Enough for a little for everyone, or a lot for the top two.
Semyon closed a big deal and wants his name on the office wall. The landlord forbids touching the walls.
Gleb and Timur haven't spoken in a week. The cause: someone ate the last cookie during code review.
Kirill proposes an internal hackathon: two days where everyone builds whatever they want. The product stops for two days.
You're doing one-on-ones. Danya says everything's great. His eyes say otherwise.
Vika wants a quiet room to work in. The only free one is the meeting room used for investor calls.
Picking a team outing: an "Escape the Office" quest room or a picnic. The quest costs three times more.
Ksyusha wants to learn "how to be a manager." She got two interns, and both do whatever they like.
left: Give her a book and time

text: A new developer asks if he can bring his dog. The cat will clearly object.
Someone set a 3 p.m. rooster alarm in the office and left. It goes off every day.
You open this week's calendar: 31 meetings plus four "thinking time" slots. Someone has booked over all four.
An intern accidentally emailed every client "test test test." Five replied "test received."
Timur suggests giving the team access to the financials. "We're adults and want to know."
The team party. The host asks the founder for a toast. You didn't prepare anything.
At the party you're called up to sing. You sing like a broken printer. The team is chanting your name.
Tonight Danya admits he spent the whole year afraid of being fired. It never crossed your mind.
Liza texts tonight: "I miss the old office." Attaches a photo of the five of you in the basement.
Friday, 7 p.m.: only you and a new hire, who's afraid to leave before the boss does.
right: Tell him he's free to go

text: Someone accidentally posts a voice note of snoring to the chat tonight. Two hundred reactions in ten minutes.
Your mentor asks tonight: "Do you have a friend outside work?" You think for a long time.
Leaving last, you find notes on the desks: "Thanks for this year." The team left them secretly.
At home they ask how the party went. You talk for an hour, all about the team. "And what about you?"
Tonight the cat brought a mouse to your desk. Apparently it's a bonus.
A candidate you really wanted turns you down tonight: "You're too fun. I'm looking for stability."
At family dinner, Mom reveals she gave hedgehog T-shirts to all the neighbors. They wear them to buy bread.
Danya sends a link tonight: his article about your product hit the top of a big developer site. He's very proud.
At 11 p.m. Kirill launches a poll: "What should our motto be?" By midnight the leader is "Sleeping is work too."
An investor drops by unannounced and finds the team playing table tennis at 3 p.m.
The board wants the quarterly report with forecasts. Alla is on vacation, and you've never seen her spreadsheets.
The lead investor invites you to dinner "just to chat." Over dessert he asks if you've considered selling.
Tonight you need to tell the board the quarterly plan was missed. How do you break it?
Time to raise again. Alla says: "Nine months of cash. A round takes six. We start yesterday."
Kirill built the new deck. 48 slides and an animation of the hedgehog riding a rocket.
You're writing a cold email to a big fund. First line: "You don't know us, but…" Sounds like a scam opener.
Vera promises an intro to a major investor — if you come to her jubilee on Saturday and give a toast.
Pitch at 8 a.m. in a café. The investor is 40 minutes late and brought his kid. The kid wants to see the hedgehog.
You discover the "active users" metric counted anyone who received a notification. The real number is half.
Gosha won't come to pitches: "That's your thing, I'm the code guy." Every investor asks where the technical co-founder is.
Video pitch at 9:00. Behind you, a wall with "DON'T PANIC" written in marker. No time to erase it.
A fund replies: "We only invest in companies that don't need money." You read it three times.
A week of five pitches a day. This morning your voice sounds like a creaky door. First pitch in an hour.
Timur asks if there'll be stock options for new hires after the round. He wants to bring in two strong people.
A term sheet arrives from a fund you don't love. Good money. So-so people.
Out for a run, you pass an investor you pitched yesterday. He's faster.
Mom sends a newspaper clipping: "How to Find an Investor: 10 Tips." Tip #1: "Smile."
Kirill suggests hiring a fundraising adviser for a cut of the round. Not a small cut.
