The fund wants a data room: every contract, report and minutes. Half the contracts are in Gosha's email.
The fund's lawyers find the hedgehog trademark is registered not to the company but to Liza.
right: Ask her to give it over

text: An investor asks: "What happens if your co-founder leaves tomorrow?" Gosha is sitting right there.
A rival's founder invites you to lunch and proposes a merger before raising: "Together we're worth more."
An investor wants you to personally answer a 120-question form. Question 87: "Describe yourself in three years in one word."
Post-pitch feedback: "Great team, boring market." Your market is beauty salons.
left: Pitch the market with more flair

text: At lunch Gosha learns that after the new round your stakes dilute to 30%. "So we work for strangers now?"
Demo for the fund. The app runs perfectly — suspiciously so. Danya whispers: "I turned on demo mode."
Ksyusha wants to post "How We're Raising Our Round," failures included. Honest and funny.
The fund partner leaves after 15 minutes, leaving a junior analyst. The analyst is trying very hard.
Two funds will invest. One offers a high valuation and harsh terms. The other: lower, but humane.
Between pitches you lunched from a vending machine: a snack bar and a soda. Next pitch in ten minutes.
Time to allocate the option pool. Everyone on the team believes they deserve more than the next person.
Arseny writes out of the blue: "I'm at a fund that's looking at you. I can put in a word." He didn't leave on good terms.
The fund wants to see the office. It's being renovated; everyone works from the café across the street.
right: Tidy the office in a rush

text: The fund wants to talk to customers. Your happiest one is a hairdresser who distrusts phones.
Timur and Gosha argue about rewriting the code before the round "so we're not embarrassed." The fund won't look at the code.
Tonight's tally: 37 meetings, 31 rejections, 6 "thinking about it." You want to lie down and never get up.
Gosha sends a meme tonight: the hedgehog hauling a sack of money. Caption: "Soon." First laugh you've had all week.
An investor sets a 9 p.m. meeting at his gym: "We'll talk on the treadmill." You're in a suit.
At home you're asked to explain the round "in simple terms." You spend an hour using spoons and plates.
11 p.m. An investor: "Got five minutes?" Five minutes turn into an hour.
For the first time in a week you open a book instead of the investor spreadsheet. Two pages in.
The team sends a support video tonight: everyone says they believe in the round. The cat makes a cameo.
A fund that turned you down a month ago calls tonight: "We changed our minds. Still open?"
You dream you're signing the round but the pen only writes "no." You wake at 3:00.
Gleb texts tonight: "If the round doesn't close, I'll work for options." You're deeply moved.
right: Promise it won't come to that

text: Friday night, the team's going to the movies. They invite you, but you have "one more investor email."
The downstairs neighbor complains you pace the apartment every evening on the phone. "It sounds like an elephant."
right: Take the calls at the office

text: You eat dinner away from the laptop for once and discover soup has flavor.
You're drafting tonight's investor newsletter. One piece of news: "Still alive, growing 4%."
10 p.m., the office lights are on. Danya's building a demo for tomorrow's fund. Nobody asked him to.
You declared an investor-free evening. An hour later you're mentally answering their questions in the shower.
Your last clean shirt for pitch week has a coffee stain shaped like a hedgehog. No time to wash.
Liza learns the hedgehog trademark in her name is worth something. She sweetly asks how much.
You look at your to-do list this morning and feel nothing. No dread, no joy. Just gray fog.
Timur notices you've worn the same expression for three days. "Coffee together? No work talk."
You bought a bike to commute. Today's day one. 12 km and one big hill.
Nobody can watch your nephew, and your sister asks if you can take him to the office for half a day. He's six and loves buttons.
You read that founders write three pages of thoughts every morning. Page one consists entirely of the word "coffee."
7 a.m., Gosha calls: "I dreamed we shut down. We didn't, right?" He sounds scared.
For the first time in two years you ask yourself when your vacation is. No answer. The calendar is full till winter.
Vika asks why you always reply to messages at 2 a.m. "It scares the team."
You skipped the alarm for the first time in a year. Woke at 9:30, rested and panicking.
A neighbor at the elevator: "You've lost so much weight! Is it the business?" It wasn't on purpose.
You signed up for morning yoga. The instructor says: "Let all thoughts go." Your thoughts refuse.
Kirill opens the morning meeting: "How do you feel, 1 to 10?" Everyone says 7. You're a 3.
You realize you drink six cups a day. Today's limit: two. It's 10 a.m. and you're yawning.
Gosha brings you a printout: "Founders' Vacation Schedule." Your name is on next week.
A friend who's a therapist suggests doing one thing a week just for its own sake. Like painting.
A courier delivers a huge box: half-asleep last night, you ordered a massage chair. Same-day returns only.
You've started walking meetings in the park. First up: Gleb, in patent leather shoes.
First proper café lunch in a month. At the next table: an investor.
Kirill says: "Hand me the clients, you're carrying everything." You're not sure he can handle it.
By mid-afternoon your head is pounding. Someone offers a break and the couch. The break looks appealing.
left: Lie down for half an hour

text: Your partner shows up at the office with a surprise lunch. You're in a meeting.
right: Ask them to wait an hour

text: Danya asks for a month of unpaid leave to "reboot."
Gosha finds out you haven't vacationed in two years and threatens to "revoke your access." He seems serious.
Vika proposes a "mood wall" in the office: everyone posts an emoji. Your emoji has been sad for three days.
The team wants a weekly football game. You'd love to, but you're sure you'll be the worst player.
You left the team chat for a day. An hour later Kirill calls: "You're not in the chat! Everything OK?"
Mid-afternoon you realize you've spent three hours redoing one spreadsheet. It was fine two hours ago.
Marina asks you along to a meeting "so the client sees the boss." Third time this week.
right: Teach Marina to be the boss

text: Ksyusha learns you loved drawing as a kid and sets up an easel in the office. "For you. Five minutes a day."
The company health checkup is at noon. A client call at 12:30.
The office is so loud you go work in your car in the parking lot. An hour later you notice Gleb and Timur are out there too.
Alla notices you're paying for everyone's coffee out of pocket. "That's not right."
You shut the laptop at 6 p.m. for the first time in a year. Now you're home and don't know what to do.
A new tradition is proposed: dinner out every Wednesday. Wednesday is fund-report day.
Your new rule: no screens after 10 p.m. It's 9:58 and an email from Gosha arrives: "URGENT!"
Friends invite you to board games tonight. You haven't seen them in six months. They're not sure you'll show.
You run a bath to relax. Ten minutes in, you're debating quarterly strategy with yourself.
left: Get out and write it down

text: You're reading a novel, not a business book, for the first time in two years. On page five the hero founds a startup.
Timur sends a video of himself learning guitar. "Maybe you'll start something too?"
You're making dinner yourself. The recipe says 30 minutes. It's been ninety, and the kitchen is covered in flour.
A former corporate colleague calls tonight: "They laid us all off. Are you still hiring?"
You did get a dog. The evening walk is the only half hour you don't think about work.
The upstairs neighbors are partying on a Wednesday. You pitch tomorrow. Bang on the radiator?
Gosha texts tonight: "I've started seeing a therapist. I recommend it." You've been thinking about it for ages.
The whole neighborhood loses power for the evening. Laptop dead, phone at 10%. Home is quiet and dark.
Tonight you're writing New Year cards for the team. On the third you realize you don't know what Gleb likes.
Out of the shower, lying down, you realize you didn't check metrics all day. The world didn't end.
A founder friend tells you tonight her startup has shut down. She's calm, even happy. You don't know what to say.
At night you wonder: "If it all ended tomorrow, would I regret it?" The answer is surprisingly calm: no.
right: Get up and write it down

text: Vika leaves a plate of apples on your desk with a note: "Food for the founder. Not for the cat." The cat is already sniffing.
An ad agency wants to buy your "anonymized" salon-booking data. Good money. Users don't know.
Kirill suggests burying the cancel-subscription button: "Churn will drop by a third."
Turns out the app sent reminders a day late all week. Two hundred people showed up on the wrong day.
Ksyusha shows you someone posting identical bad reviews under different names. Suspicion falls on a rival.
Users want a tipping feature for stylists. It's hard to build and earns you nothing.
On the stand-up Danya proposes deleting half the features "nobody uses." Gosha wrote every one.
A support agent is in tears this morning: a user called her a robot. "I'm a person!"
A hobbyist hacker writes: "Found a hole in your system. I'll tell you for a reward." Might be true.
The app marketplace rejected your update: "The hedgehog resembles another logo." Whose, they won't say.
Gleb shows that rewriting search would make the app 30% faster. Two weeks and silence needed.
You gave a beta to twenty stylists. One writes: "Everything broke, but I love it."
You notice 80% of revenue comes from 5% of clients. One of them is threatening to leave.
You launched a team idea contest. This morning: 14 slips in the box. Six are about the cat.
Kirill wants a paid "Premium" tier with a gold hedgehog. The free hedgehog would turn gray.
The cat walked across Danya's keyboard this morning and accidentally closed a week-long task. It got fixed.
Your app made a "Best for Small Business" list. Users doubled. The servers are groaning.
A user says he was charged twice. True — a billing bug. He threatens to go to the press.
You let users vote on the next feature. The winner: "Hedgehog dances when you book."
A big client wants a feature to track how long stylists spend on breaks.
You spent a day in a salon watching stylists. They use the app wearing gloves — the buttons are too small.
Gosha found out Danya wants to delete his features and took offense. The chat is silent.
A journalist writes: "We have a screenshot of your internal chat discussing a client." It was a joking chat.
An elderly stylist calls just to say: "Thank you for the big font." The call lasts twenty minutes.
The board demands ads in the free version. Users in surveys are against it.
Danya built something nobody asked for: the app reminds stylists to drink water. Everyone loves it.
A blogger calls you "the most boring app of the year." Ksyusha wants to make it the slogan.
Timur shows a chart: development speed dropped threefold because of old code. Needs a month of cleanup.
A rival proposes merging stylist databases: "Together we're stronger." His is five times smaller.
At 2 p.m. the hedgehog flips upside down for every user. Nobody knows why. Users love it.
You asked users what they love about the app. Top answer: "Support that talks like a human."
Liza proposes building for stylists, not salon owners: "Stylists are our real users."
Vika drew a beautiful new screen, but Gleb says it can't be built. They've argued for an hour.
11 p.m., a payment failure: money is charged but bookings aren't created. Danya's on call and scared.
A stylist whose data was stolen from another service writes tonight: "You wouldn't do that, right?" You don't know how to answer briefly.
Gosha admits tonight half his features really are useless. "But I loved them."
Reading comments on an article about you tonight. Twenty kind, one nasty. You reread the nasty one for the sixth time.
Vika texts: "Can I work noon to 8? I'm not human in the mornings."
You're told: "You're always on your phone. Even during a show you're watching your phone."
left: Leave the phone in another room

text: Tonight you realize the monthly security report for users hasn't gone out in six months. You promised monthly.
A stylist writes tonight: "Thanks to you I took my first vacation in ten years — the app handles bookings."
left: Read it to the team tomorrow

text: You can't sleep because you've figured out how to make booking two clicks instead of three.
right: Get up and mock it up

text: That hobbyist hacker writes again tonight: "You patched it? Nice. Want me to check monthly?"
Tonight in the user chat someone posts their cat in a hedgehog T-shirt. Dozens more follow.
Danya admits tonight that the "dancing hedgehog" winner was his — he voted 300 times.
Cleaning up email tonight, you find a six-month-old message from a client: "Ready to buy for the whole chain."
Tonight you remember snapping at Kirill in the morning meeting. He was quiet all day.
A new remote developer from another city writes tonight: "I still can't tell who's in charge."
Mom calls: her hairdresser friend uses your app and "loves it, but the hedgehog is weird."
You dream the app runs perfectly, the team is happy and you sleep eight hours. You wake up — and it's almost true.
Timur and Gleb, recently at odds, are having tea together in the office kitchen. You see them through the glass.
A client salon wants an app workshop for twenty stylists. Saturday. Morning.
Knee-deep snow overnight. Half the team can't get in; the other half is building a snow hedgehog in the yard.
Two weeks to New Year. The board wants Premium launched "before the holidays." The team wants holidays.
Ksyusha brought a tree into the office. The cat considers it his property and has knocked it over twice.
Time to choose New Year gifts for clients. Chocolate hedgehogs, or cards hand-drawn by the team?
You organized Secret Santa and drew Gleb. All you know is his love of code review.
right: Gift a book on code review

text: The morning after the New Year party. Three people in, all drinking water by the liter. Client meeting at 10.
Gosha arrives in a Santa suit: "I'm handing out bonuses." There are no bonuses this year.
The board wants a year-end deck by Friday. You open the calendar and realize the year passed like one long Monday.
First warm day. The team wants the stand-up on the building's roof. Not allowed, but so tempting.
right: Hold it in the meeting room

text: The office is sweltering. You bought fans, but there are three for ten people. Who gets them?
Autumn blues hit half the team. Vika proposes an "autumn club" with morning cocoa.
Two years to the day since you left corporate. In the office, there's a poster of you from the basement days.
You're late to your own meeting because your cat locked you in the bathroom by knocking over a mop.
In August half the team wants the same week off. The product won't survive it.
The office clock stopped. Nobody noticed for three days. Does that say something about the culture?
Building management sends a new rule: "No animals." The cat looks at you.
Ksyusha accidentally sent the New Year newsletter in March. Users reply: "Thanks, and happy holidays to you too!"
left: Joke about it in a follow-up

text: Choosing the year-end party. Gosha wants a costume ball, Gleb wants "just a quiet dinner." The budget says dinner.
A client sent a huge fruit basket for New Year. The note: "Looking forward to next year's discount."
The cat got more New Year cards than the whole staff combined. Gleb is jealous.
In summer, the building owner turned off the AC "to save money." The team proposes working from the park.
At the summer team picnic Gosha decided to grill. It's charcoal. Hungry colleagues look at you.
right: Eat bread and joke about it

text: It's Danya's one-year anniversary. He thinks nobody remembers. Everyone does and is planning a 3 p.m. surprise.
left: Cut the meeting short for it

text: For your anniversary Gosha suggests going "back to the roots": a week working from your kitchen.
Friday the 13th. Gleb refuses to deploy "for superstitious reasons." You have an important release.
April 1. Ksyusha wants to announce the app is now cats-only.
Kirill proposes a Black Friday deal: 70% off. Alla nearly faints at the number.
Gosha asks to go to a conference somewhere warm. The theme: blockchain for bakeries.
Vera hints that the board would appreciate New Year gifts.
You started a weekly team breakfast. The first one: just you and the pancakes.
Kirill organized team building: build a tower out of spaghetti. Gosha and Gleb are already fighting about the tower's architecture.
On Valentine's Day, someone anonymously left hedgehog valentines on every desk. Suspicion falls on Liza.
It's freezing in the office. Everyone works in blankets, and the cat sleeps on the server because it's warm.
At the anniversary Gosha awards you a cardboard medal: "For Survival." It's touching and a bit sad.
December 31, 10 p.m. The server's up, the team's home. Your first holiday without a laptop in two years. Almost.
First January holidays. You woke at noon and don't know what to do with yourself. Your hands reach for the laptop.
At the year-end party Gosha toasts: "To a more boring next year." Everyone raises their juice and laughs.
left: Add a toast of your own

text: Your parents ask tonight if you're coming for the holidays. The board wants a call on January 2.
Tonight you write your own year in review. "Rested" is blank. "Grew" is long.
The team gives you a spa voucher tonight with a note: "Please don't open the laptop there."
Sunday, 8 p.m. You scroll old photos: the basement, the kitchen, the first thousand users. It warms your heart.
right: Make an album for the office

text: Summer evening, the team invites you to the roof for the sunset. You promised yourself to finish the quarterly plan.
Rainy autumn evening. Just you and the cat in the office. He looks at you like he knows about the runway.
At the dacha, a neighbor learns you're a "startup person" and asks you to review his idea: a greenhouse with an app.
Liza sends a festive hedgehog in a hat with lights. "Can we make it the holiday app icon?"
December 30, evening: a client calls: "Holiday bookings at our salon, everything's broken!" The team has scattered.
On your anniversary evening you and Gosha sit in the kitchen where it all began. He asks: "Two more years?"
The night before the Premium launch. You toss and turn imagining it all breaking.
Friday, the team's gone. A note on your desk: "Please leave before 8 p.m. — The Team."
Evening snowstorm. You're stuck in the office with Gleb and the cat. Only tea and cookies.
For the first time you're getting yourself a New Year gift. A new work chair or theater tickets?
New Year's night, the neighbors set off fireworks. In their glow you see 14 unread messages from Kirill.
A morning email from a big company in a neighboring industry: they want to buy you outright. You count the zeros three times.
Gosha reads the acquisition offer and is silent for five minutes. Then: "I'd buy a house by the sea. But I'd miss the hedgehog."
Rumor of the buyout has reached the team. At the stand-up every camera is on, and everyone's looking at you.
The buyer wants an office tour this morning. The cat is asleep on the meeting room table, and a "DON'T PANIC" poster is on the wall.
The lawyer warns: under the deal terms you'd have to stay with the new company for three years. No early exit.
Timur says: "If you sell, I'll stay — as long as there's no dress code." That's his main condition.
right: Say it's not up to you

text: Alla brings a spreadsheet: if you sell, everyone gets an options payout. For some it's a year's salary.
You walk to the office to think about the sale. Twenty minutes later you realize you've overshot it by three blocks.
Vera calls at 7:30: "Sell! I've waited ten years for this." Easy for her — she's the angel.
Kirill admits he's already interviewed at the acquiring company "just in case."
News of the possible sale hits the press. Users write this morning: "You won't ruin the app, will you?"
You wake at 5:00 and realize that, for once, you don't want anything to change. You like things as they are.
Danya leaves a drawing on your desk: the hedgehog in a corporate suit, captioned "Please don't."
Someone left a cactus on your desk with a note: "Hang in there." Anonymous.
The acquirer's CEO suggests breakfast at 7:00 at his country club.
A founder friend who sold says: "Don't sell the first time. I regret it." Another friend says the opposite.
The morning after a sleepless night of thinking. The team has made breakfast "to make your decision easier."
The board votes 3–2 to sell. The deciding votes are yours and Gosha's as founders.
The buyer wants to rename the product "Booking Service 3.0." No hedgehog.
Hearing about the offer, a fund proposes a new round instead: "Don't sell, keep growing."
You and Gosha lunch at the canteen by the old basement where it all started. The buckwheat hasn't changed.
Gleb says: "I don't care who owns us, as long as nobody touches the code." He's the only calm person in the office.
left: Ask him to talk to the team

text: Marina reports two big clients will leave if you're bought. They dislike the acquirer.
Mid-negotiation you slip out to the restroom and stare in the mirror for five minutes. You look tired, but alive.
The buyer offers you the title "Chief Innovation Officer" with a car and driver. You ride a scooter.
Ksyusha asks to film a documentary about the sale. "It's history!"
At lunch Gosha suddenly says: "I'm against it. Let's go one more year on our own." You feel relief.
right: Ask him to think till Friday

text: The buyer suggests "signing today and sorting out the details later." The details are the team's future.
Timur suggests a compromise: sell only the technology, keep the team and the hedgehog.
right: Say it doesn't work that way

text: A journalist asks: "Is it true you turned down the buyer over a hedgehog?" Almost true.
After you turn down the sale, the board demands a plan to double revenue in a year. Meeting in an hour.
After your refusal, the would-be buyer offers to rent you a floor below market. "No hard feelings."
9 p.m. The buyer needs an answer by midnight. Gosha's on the phone; the team is waiting in the chat.
You turned down the buyer. Tonight the team chat is hundreds of hedgehogs and one message from Gleb: "Right call."
At home: "So we turned down a house by the sea?" You explain about the hedgehog. They seem to understand.
Vera calls tonight, upset: "I was counting on that sale." Her stake could have been her retirement.
right: Offer to buy out her stake

text: You lie awake wondering if you made the right call. The cat climbs on top of you. Is that an answer?
Kirill writes tonight that he's accepted an offer from the would-be buyer. "Nothing personal, it's my career."
Gosha sends a photo tonight: a hedgehog drawn on his kitchen whiteboard, captioned "One more year."
left: Hang the photo in the office

text: Mom heard you turned down the deal from the news. "You turned down money because of a hedgehog?" She doesn't get it but she's proud.
First unhurried dinner of the week. Phone on silent. The world didn't end.
Semyon texts tonight: your biggest client renewed for two years after hearing you won't sell.
Alla sends a new plan tonight: revenue can double, but it means six months of weekend work.
You write in your journal: "Turned down big money today. Scary, but calm."
11:30 p.m.: three emails from funds: "Heard you didn't sell. Let's talk."
The team gathers outside the office tonight with a banner: "Thanks for staying."
Dad says tonight: "At your age I turned down a job too. Never regretted it." It's the first time he's ever mentioned it.
Your sock-app neighbor congratulates you: "Read about you! Now will you invest in my startup?"
Tonight you open a blank doc: "Year Three Plan." First line: "Remember to rest."
Moving day. The movers arrived at 8:00 and none of the boxes are labeled. One of them may contain the cat.
You're giving students an 8:30 a.m. lecture on startups. They're there for credit, but one asks questions like an investor.
Gosha confesses: he wants to stop being a "director" and just write code again. "It makes me happier."
right: Ask him to hang on a year

text: Vika bought a robot vacuum. Every morning it gets stuck under your desk and beeps plaintively during calls.
right: Name it and put up with it

text: Only Gleb knows the new office Wi-Fi password. He's on vacation and not answering. The whole team is on your phone hotspot.
Liza shares happy news: in six months she's going on parental leave. She's nervous about how you'll react.
9:00, a fire drill. The whole building is out on the street. You have a fund video call in ten minutes.
Your first user meetup. Eight stylists came, plus a man who got the wrong address. He's staying.
You launched an internship program. Five interns arrived, all asking at once where to get a laptop.
The building elevator is broken. The office is on the ninth floor. An important elderly client is on his way.
left: Meet him at the café downstairs

text: It's your birthday. You hoped nobody would remember, but the office is already full of hedgehog balloons.
You drove to the office for the first time. The only free spot is paid; the free ones are two blocks away.
The podcast where you talked "about failures" comes out at 8:00. Listening back, you realize you sound like a happy person.
A school class comes for a tour. They ask whether it's true you can sleep at work in a startup.
Timur notices your third energy drink of the morning and silently swaps it for water.
Danya invites the whole team to his wedding on Saturday. You'd planned a strategy session for Saturday.
right: Move the session, skip the wedding

text: The new CTO starts today, replacing Gosha. Gosha picked him himself and is now watching jealously.
right: Let the new guy settle in alone

text: Users suggest crowdfunding a new feature: "We'll pay, just build it."
Alla proposes health insurance for staff. Expensive, but the team has asked for ages.
A laptop vanished from the office. The cameras show a courier took it, mixing up packages. He's bringing it back.
A young rival's founder asks for advice: "How do I survive year one?" He copies you, but endearingly.
A visually impaired user writes she can't use the app. Fixing it properly will take a month.
The messaging service you use for reminders went down. Not your fault, but users are angry at you.
The new CTO invites everyone to lunch on him, "to get acquainted." Gosha won't go.
A publisher wants you to write a book about the startup. Six months. In the evenings.
Vika proposes a quarterly volunteer day: the team helps an animal shelter. The cat approves.
A barbershop in a small village wants to sign up, but the only internet there is at the post office.
The new printer works perfectly, but only after you say hello to it. Literally — Gleb configured it that way.
The board suggests hiring you a "founder's assistant" to free up your time. You have no idea what to delegate.
Gosha, back to being just a programmer, laughs at code review for the first time in a year. The new CTO asks if he's always like this.
right: Ask Gosha to mentor the new guy

text: A stylist mailed you a handwritten letter. Inside: a pressed flower.
The bank approved your mortgage once they saw the company is profitable. Signing is during work hours.
An intern asks if he can skip meetings because "they talk about things I don't understand."
right: Let him read the notes instead

text: You're interviewing a candidate who worked at your old corporation. He sat at your old desk.
You're the last in the office again. The building guard brings you tea: "I'm always last too."
Your partner puts on a startup sitcom and laughs: "That's you!" It's funny and a little hurtful.
The new CTO texts tonight: "Gosha's code is art. Terrifying, but art."
Tonight Liza sends an ultrasound photo: her baby "already looks like a hedgehog." The whole team is tearing up in the chat.
You finished a book for the first time in a year. You want to tell everyone, but they're asleep.
right: Tell the team in the morning

text: Tonight you realize that for the first time in three years, opening the banking app doesn't scare you.
The friend who shut her startup invites you to dinner. She's starting a new one and wants you as an adviser.
11 p.m., Gosha calls: "I just wanted to say I'm happy right now." He hangs up.
Driving home, you pass your old corporate office. Your former department's windows are still lit.
Tonight you list what you'd tell yourself three years ago at the kitchen table. Item one: "Sleep."
right: Pin it up in the office

text: At dinner your friends' kids ask what you want to be when you grow up. You actually think about it.
For once you arrive at family dinner on time. Mom checks, just in case, that you're not ill.
The cat you took home brings you a sock tonight. Maybe it's a hint about your sock-app neighbor.
Tonight you're booking a two-week vacation. Your finger has hovered over "Pay" for five minutes.
Tonight you open the task board and see you have only five tasks. The team took the rest.
Vera sends a voice note tonight: "Sorry about that call. I'm proud you didn't sell."
Friday, 6 p.m. The team heads home on time. You look at the empty office and switch off the lights too.
You write a letter to your future self, to open in a year. First line: "Do you still rest on weekends?"
Late tonight you sit at the very kitchen table where it all began. Gosha texts: "So, next startup?"
You dream of day one: leaving corporate, and the turnstile guard says, "Good luck." You wake up smiling.
Ksyusha ordered a thousand hedgehog stickers. A week later they're on every laptop, every door and possibly the cat.
A weekend out of town: for the first time in three years you're looking at the stars. The phone has one bar.
